name: Lithuania: participant-facing document QC
item_format: Each result records the item id, the outcome, a short rationale and evidence (quoted passage and source locator) or an explicit gap.

items.check: Trial purpose and research nature are stated; the investigational treatment is not presented as proven to help.
Investigational treatment and comparator named and described as in the protocol and IB/SmPC.
Randomisation and blinding explained correctly in plain language.
Number and timing of visits match the schedule of activities.
Invasive and burdensome procedures are described.
Treatment duration and follow-up match the protocol.
Prohibited and required concomitant treatments are stated.
Reproductive precautions match the protocol.
Safety monitoring is described.
Withdrawal and early discontinuation procedures match the protocol.
No visit schedule, dose, comparator or follow-up period different from the protocol; no statements carried over from another protocol, country, cohort or phase.

sections.title: Protocol-to-participant-document consistency
sections.instruction: Check every participant-facing statement that can be traced to the protocol.

items.check: Eligibility-related participant obligations match the protocol.
Procedures and assessments match the protocol; research-only procedures are visible.
Sample collection volumes and frequency match the protocol and sample plan.
Imaging and radiation match the protocol.
Questionnaires, diaries and digital tools match the protocol.
Home visits or decentralised elements are described; home visits are treated as exceptional and described in the protocol and consent documentation, especially where optional.
Pregnancy testing and contraception periods match the protocol.
Optional substudies are described as optional and match the protocol.
Data and sample retention periods match the protocol and are consistent across documents.
Follow-up after treatment discontinuation matches the protocol.
After a protocol change, every affected participant document has been reopened.
The consent needed to join and remain in the main trial is clearly separate from optional choices (for example future research use of samples or coded data).
Refusing an optional activity does not read as disqualifying the person from the main trial, unless the protocol genuinely makes it essential.
Consent is described as voluntary, informed, documented and obtained before trial-specific participation, unless a lawful special pathway applies.
The right to refuse or withdraw and what happens to data already collected after withdrawal are explained.
The person signing has legal authority for the decision; the basis of representation is recorded when someone else consents.
Electronic consent uses a signature method whose legal validity is established; a simple electronic signature is not treated as equivalent to a handwritten one.
The consent form does not introduce information absent from the information sheet.

sections.title: Population and document coverage
sections.instruction: Map each protocol population to the correct information and consent documents (requirements.json population_sets).

items.check: Every inclusion pathway in the protocol maps to a population with its full document set; populations are mutually exclusive within each consent stage.
Healthy volunteers: no implied therapeutic benefit; payment, reimbursement, risks and free trial procedures clearly explained; screen-failure data handling covered.
Minors: age group (under 12 or 12 and above), both-parent signature logic with documented exceptions, assent from 12 when capable, dissent, and re-consent at adulthood.

Limited-capacity adults: the legally entitled consent-giver is defined under Lithuanian law, the participant receives adapted information and dissent is addressed; re-consent when capacity is regained.
Emergency enrolment: Article 35 is met and the documents explain how consent to continue is obtained without undue delay, later refusal and the right to object to use of data.
Impartial witness: witness pathway for inability to write (not lack of capacity), reason for its use and signature block present.
Pregnancy follow-up: the person providing pregnancy data is correctly identified as the trial participant or the participant's partner; consent and privacy logic match that person.
Future use of samples or coded data: separate future-use ICF or a distinct opt-in choice; refusal does not affect main-trial participation.

sections.title: Data privacy
sections.instruction: Participant-facing privacy information is consistent with the sponsor's GDPR statement (LT-R1) and the actual data flows.

items.check: Controller identity and contact route where required.
Categories of personal and health data.
Source of the data.
Access by sponsor, monitors, auditors and authorities.
Coding or pseudonymisation.
Recipients and international transfers.
items.applies_when: data transferred to recipients outside the site or outside the EEA

items.check: Storage period.
Use after withdrawal.
Rights and complaint routes.
Special categories such as genetics, race or ethnicity are named when collected; race or ethnicity collection is scientifically justified and transparently explained.
Trial consent is not used as a catch-all permission for every future data use.
Purpose in the main trial for each sample.
Collection timing.
Where analysis occurs.
Storage and destruction plan.
Whether future use is planned.
Whether future use is optional.
Whether withdrawal from future use is explained, and what still happens to completed analyses, datasets, distributed samples and anonymised information.

Future-use information covers purposes, storage duration and location and personal data issues, and as relevant coding, access, recipients, transfers, commercial research, genetic analysis and return of results.
Sample types, storage locations, retention, future-use purpose, transfers and destruction agree with the S1 biological-sample compliance form.
The participant documents are in Lithuanian.
The recruitment and consent procedure (K1) covers the actual consent pathway of this document.
Advertisements are submitted with the supporting explanation the Lithuanian Bioethics Committee expects (need, placement, ineligible respondents, reimbursement, respondents' personal data).
Reimbursement and compensation wording agrees with the financial submission (P1, P2); an approximate hourly amount is stated when time is compensated.
The participant information states that the investigational medicinal product and trial health checks are free of charge, where applicable.
Contraception costs are handled consistently (compensated) where contraception is required specifically because of the trial.
Biological-sample compliance information (S1) is included when applicable.
Insurance or indemnification arrangements and how to seek compensation for trial-related harm match the submitted certificate or policy (LT-O1).
A person who does not understand Lithuanian is consented only through the pathway defined in advance in K1.
The ICF version number and date match the document register.
The Lithuanian version corresponds to the intended master version.
All signature blocks are appropriate for the population.
The representative basis is captured when someone else gives consent.
Witness fields exist only where the pathway may be used.
The participant and interviewer have not pre-signed the initial submission ICF.
Signature fields include names, signatures, date and time; the participant's copy is also signed by the investigator or authorised research person.
Filenames and document titles distinguish population and use case clearly; CTIS title follows the naming guide.
No drafting instruction remains (content/conventions/template-instructions.md).

sections.title: Readability and translation
sections.instruction: Read the Lithuanian text as a participant would, not as a translator would.

items.check: Sentences are short enough to follow.
Technical terms are explained.
Risks use consistent plain-language wording.
Optional choices are visibly separate.
Headings make the document easy to scan.
The document does not contradict itself about withdrawal, data or samples.
The translation preserves the regulatory meaning of the source without sounding literal.
Protocol, consent pathway, Lithuanian wording, privacy statements, optional choices, signatures and version control all agree.
The participant document list matches the protocol's populations and the Lithuania Part II package checklist.
